purpose: Static architecture viability review for staging the BUG-086 callable helper pack in physical page $34. No source changes or runtime probe were made for this review.

copy_table.interpretation: The existing copy record already selects a physical destination page and address. One contiguous helper target needs one additional record; fragmented source assignment may need more, up to six records under this snapshot.

projected_after_one_87_byte_target.assumption: The 87-byte helper image maps from one contiguous source interval and therefore adds one descriptor. The final generator manifest must prove the actual segmentation.

existing_page34_executable_target.interpretation: Confirms that the current generic boot copy protocol already stages executable bytes to physical page $34. The new all-profile helper payload would be a separate generated target.

gate_transition_alias.source: src/main.s draw_gate_transition maps PAR5 to GATE_TRANSITION_PAGE=$39 before reading GATE_TRANSITION_PAYLOAD and restores $34 before calling draw_gate_entities.

physical_page34_ranges.writer_clear_audit: Current source has no physical-page-$34 writer or bulk clear over $A8A0-$A8FC. Existing initialization writes the maze only through $A23F, gates through $A253, entity/enemy records in their declared extents, the ring at $A898-$A89B, and the three candidate state bytes. Framebuffer initialization maps PAR5 to pages $2C-$2F for framebuffer copies, then initializes ledgers at $A900 and $AA00.

projected_enemy_fit.call_site_change: draw_enemy_stage BSR (2 bytes) becomes LBSR (3 bytes) to page-$34 helper.
projected_enemy_fit.result_kind: Projection from current candidate assembly and retained adaptive listing, not an emitted all-profile result.
hard_bounds_retained: enemy executable/module end remains at or below $17A0 before the LUT
all executable/data remains below active-stage RAM at $1800
resident guard remains below $E000 in both profiles
helper bytes remain below logo state at $A8FD
immutable asset end remains at or below $FE00

par5_lifetime_audit.boot_delivery: The existing sparse-copy loop reads each descriptor's destination page, maps it in PAR5, and copies to the descriptor's $A000-$BFFF destination address. It already uses page $34 for adaptive_helper at $BD44. The proposed helper uses the same record format and copy loop; src/gmc_bootstrap.s does not need a protocol or resident-code change.
par5_lifetime_audit.normal_selector: enemy_release_impl calls the normal selector through the enemy module while gameplay PAR5 is $34. Stage/gameplay re-entry explicitly sets $34 before shared initialization and foreground game state access.
par5_lifetime_audit.preview: draw_enemy_stage calls enemy_frame_number before sparse_enemy_stream changes PAR5. compose_enemy_animation's preview/cache checks also occur before any stream remap.
par5_lifetime_audit.cache_guard_return: The page-$34 cache guard calls the fixed low-RAM build_enemy_nest_cache vector at $0824. The builder calls draw_enemy_stage; each preview runs before the stream remap, and sparse_blit_stage restores PAR5=$34 at sparse_decode_done before returning. The low-RAM builder therefore returns to the page-$34 helper with its code page mapped.
par5_lifetime_audit.interrupt: framebuffer_irq_impl calls only the always-mapped framebuffer IRQ entry; it updates direct-page counters and display ownership but does not change PAR5. An interrupt during page-$34 helper execution returns to the same mapping.
par5_lifetime_audit.demo_and_presentation: Demo cold-route reads temporarily map a presentation cold page and restore $34 before returning. Auxiliary presentation module installation maps page $23 only for the copy and restores $34. Sparse page-$39 drawing restores $34 in its decoder completion path; gate transition explicitly restores $34 before follow-on entity work.
par5_lifetime_audit.remaining_lifetime_gate: The implementation build must prove every new LBSR target from emitted instruction bytes in both profiles and retain the page-$34 entry invariant at every helper call site. This static audit does not replace the runtime scenarios in BUG-086.

required: src/enemy_runtime.s: move enemy_frame_number out of the pre-LUT module; call the page-$34 entry with LBSR; retain state consumption and renderer ordering.
src/main.s: retain reset initialization of $A89D-$A89F; remove the 50-byte immutable helper bodies and obsolete helper placement guard/aliases.
src/enemy_helpers_page34.s: new all-profile 6809 helper source assembled at $A8A0, containing the 50-byte selector/cache helpers and 37-byte enemy_frame_number body.
scripts/build.sh: assemble the helper source for adaptive and nonadaptive profiles and pass its binary to the existing sparse asset builder.
scripts/build_sparse_sprites.py: add an 8-bit-safe bounded raw target for physical page $34 at $A8A0, with end guard $A8FD.
scripts/verify_sparse_sprites.py: whitelist and reconstruct the new target at page $34:$A8A0 with exact byte coverage and bounds.
scripts/source_reference.json: register the new authored assembly source for source provenance.
verification_touchpoints: scripts/verify_enemy_runtime.py must be updated for the moved frame selector and helper symbols.
scripts/build.sh existing sparse-table overlap guard must pass with the added generated record(s).
scripts/verify_gmc_boot.py must continue to prove descriptor bytes match the manifest; no protocol change is proposed.
loader_files_not_required_for_protocol: resident code placement or resident capacity

status_and_gates.architecture_verdict: VIABLE EXISTING-LOADER PATH FOUND: page-$34 staging uses the current generic sparse-copy descriptor, and the current asset snapshot has one-record capacity plus source-byte margin. The 87-byte package fits the proposed $A8A0-$A8FC code interval by 6 bytes and recovers 36 net enemy-module bytes by projection.

prove final descriptor count, source packing, physical page/address, and image hashes against the generated manifest
verify the nonadaptive pre-LUT guard passes with all fixed bounds preserved
decode each emitted LBSR byte displacement and compare it with the assembled target symbol
